q: In a child with whooping cough, all are true EXCEPT:
o: Higher risk of brain damage under 1 year
Erythromycin completely resolves symptoms within 10 days
e: Antibiotics shorten the period of infectivity but do not stop the cough.

q: In pertussis, all are true EXCEPT:
o: Young infants may have no whoop
Infectivity starts in the paroxysmal stage
e: The catarrhal stage is the most infectious.

q: The main cause of death in diphtheria is:
e: Myocarditis caused by the toxin, in the second to third week.

q: The most important treatment of diphtheria is:
e: Antitoxin neutralises the toxin that is not yet bound; penicillin is also given.

q: A 7-year-old has trismus and painful spasms after a wound from a nail; he is alert. What is the antibiotic of choice?
e: Metronidazole, together with human tetanus immunoglobulin, diazepam and wound care.

q: Any child under 15 with acute flaccid paralysis should have:
o: Notification and 2 stool samples 24 hours apart within 14 days
e: This is acute flaccid paralysis surveillance for polio.

q: Asymmetric flaccid leg paralysis with normal sensation after a febrile illness suggests:
e: Polio causes asymmetric paralysis with normal sensation.
